kinds.d: Living culture of wild yeast and lactic bacteria kept to leaven bread.

x.d: Starter for the sour white bread of San Francisco, whose bacterium Fructilactobacillus sanfranciscensis was named for the city.

v.d: bakery starter kept in use since 1849

v.n: Cultures for Health San Francisco Sourdough Starter

x.d: Heirloom starter said to have crossed the Oregon Trail in 1847; shared free as dried powder by Carl's Friends since 2000.
Starter tradition of Alaska and the Yukon, carried by prospectors in the 1898 Klondike Gold Rush.

kinds.d: Living culture of bacteria and yeast kept to ferment sweet tea into kombucha.

x.d: Symbiotic culture of acetic acid bacteria and yeast forming a mat on sweetened black or green tea; believed to come from China.
Kombucha-like culture brewed with green tea and honey.

kinds.d: Living culture grains kept to ferment milk into kefir.

x.d: Cauliflower-like grains of bacteria and yeasts bound in kefiran, from the North Caucasus; they enlarge and split as they are reused.

v.n: Cultures for Health Milk Kefir Starter Culture

kinds.a: tibicos · tibi · sugar kefir grains · Japanese water crystals · ginger beer plant
kinds.d: Living culture grains kept to ferment sugar water.

x.d: Translucent dextran grains of lactic bacteria and yeasts fermenting sugar water, juice or coconut water; reported from Mexican Opuntia in 1899.

v.n: Cultures for Health Water Kefir Starter Culture

v.d: grains Beijerinck linked to the Crimean War, a claim later called unsubstantiated

kinds.d: Spores of koji mould, on grain or as powder, sold to inoculate steamed rice, barley or soybeans to make koji.

x.d: Japan's 'national fungus', used for sake, miso, soy sauce, mirin and rice vinegar.

v.d: for sake, mirin and some vinegar

x.d: Koji mould used mainly for awamori and shōchū.
Mutant of black koji used for shōchū.

kinds.d: Living or freeze-dried bacterial culture kept to make yogurt at home.

x.d: Finnish and Swedish ropy, 'long' mesophilic fermented milk with a velvety Geotrichum candidum surface.

v.d: cream viili, used like sour cream

x.d: Georgian mesophilic yogurt with a thin, custard-like texture and honey notes.
Thin, drinkable, mild Scandinavian mesophilic culture.
Re-culturable set of one sachet each of Viili, Filmjölk, Matsoni and Piimä.

kinds.d: Living film of cellulose, acetic acid bacteria and yeast added to wine, cider or beer to make vinegar.

x.d: Biofilm named Mycoderma aceti by Pasteur in 1861; Beijerinck named its bacterium Acetobacter aceti in 1898.

brands.d: Online seller of home starter cultures for yogurt, kefir, kombucha, sourdough and cheese, run by Julie and Eric Feickert.
Kyoto seed-koji maker (moyashiya) recorded in 1769, the only one left in Kyoto.

traditions.d: Seed-koji merchants who keep, cultivate and sell koji mould spores to sake, miso and soy-sauce makers.
traditions.tech: koji mould grown on steamed rice with wood ash, spores sold on grain or as powder
traditions.mat: Aspergillus oryzae and related moulds; rice, barley
traditions.auth: about ten moyashiya remain in Japan; strains are chosen per product (sake, miso, shōchū)

traditions.d: Fermented milk made with kefir grains, traditionally in goatskin bags hung by the door.
traditions.tech: grains added to milk, strained and reused; grains enlarge and split
traditions.mat: cow, goat or sheep milk; kefir grains
traditions.auth: true kefir is made from grains; powdered starters do not form grains

traditions.d: Mesophilic ropy fermented milks set at room temperature.
traditions.tech: mesophilic lactic fermentation with surface Geotrichum candidum
traditions.auth: long, ropy texture and velvety mould surface
